messages:
sophia: noticed a big p99 jump on staging after the v4.4.0 model bump. rolling canary shows latency up ~2.3x and token/sec down. tagging ops.
kevin: looking now — is this the checkpoint that changed tokenizer params? there was a tokenizer.json diff in the checkpoint bundle.
sophia: yes, new checkpoint: model@v4.4.0 (checkpoint d3b9f2). tokenizer config changed: 'eos_id' shifted and `normalize_unicode` toggled. staging perf delta: p50 42ms -> 48ms, p95 120ms -> 210ms, p99 220ms -> 560ms.
marta: who ran profile traces? any kernel selector mismatches or batch size skew?
ryan: I pulled a perf trace from one noisy pod, attaching clipped logs below: ```
[2026-03-18T10:02:11Z] request id=abc123 model=v4.4.0 seq_len=128 selected_kernel=matmul_fused_q8 fastpath=false
[2026-03-18T10:02:11Z] kv_cache_hits=0 kv_cache_evictions=18 prefetch_policy=token_prefetch_v1
[2026-03-18T10:02:11Z] batch_size=1 scheduler_bucket=latency_pref
[2026-03-18T10:02:11Z] kernel_fallback=enabled reason=tokenizer_encoding_mismatch
```
sophia: interesting — kernel selected is the lower-throughput fallback. looks like tokenizer drift caused different tokenization lengths which changed kernel heuristic path.
kevin: that matches an earlier hypothesis: when tokenized length distribution shifts, our kernel selector moves to conservative kernels + disables certain prefetchers. combined with small batches, you get thrashing and KV cache churn.
marta: can we confirm kv cache metrics across the fleet? numbers on staging: kv_cache_evictions/sec spiked from 3->95 on canary nodes. also observed hot loop spin in allocator.
ryan: ran a quick bisect against runtime commits from last merge. suspecting commit 0f9a4c2 (scheduler: prefer conservative kernel on <avg_len 20) as the trigger when paired with tokenizer change.
kevin: run this locally: `python infra/perf_bisect.py --bench=staging-capture --range=0a1b2c..0f9a4c2 --model=d3b9f2` should show where latency diverged. I can run after lunch if someone else doesn't.
sophia: CI flagged a perf regression too: `eng-ci` flagged slower median for e2e smoke on the v4.4.0 snapshot.
ci-bot: PERF ALERT: pipeline=staging-e2e, metric=p99_latency, baseline=210ms, current=560ms, regression=+167%. See: https://ci.internal/reports/3012345
kevin: @marta can you pause the canary rollout? we should avoid wider impact.
marta: paused. canary traffic set to 0% for v4.4.0. rolling back also on the table.
sophia: before a full revert, can we try a temporary kernel selector tweak to prefer previous heuristic? maybe override `kernel_selector.v2.enabled=false` for the canary.
ryan: that should be quick — doing a shadow config flip on one host now. results in ~30s.
(30s pass)
ryan: flipped `kernel_selector.v2.enabled=false` on the noisy pod. p99 dropped from ~560ms -> 230ms in that pod within two minutes. kv_cache_evictions/sec back to ~4.
kevin: good signal — confirms selector+tokenizer interaction is the root cause.
sophia: next steps: 1) prod pause for v4.4.0 (we already paused canary) 2) create a hotfix that either: revert tokenizer config in checkpoint OR add tokenizer-aware exception in kernel selector 3) run full fleet bisect to be safe.
marta: opened ticket INF-4921 with rollback playbook and assign to eng-runtime and model-onboard. linking profiler dumps and the bisect command.
kevin: I'll work on a kernel-selector patch that checks token length distribution before switching to conservative kernels. if we push a patch, we should shadow it then rollout.
sophia: can someone post the exact tokenizer diff so model team can confirm if we should patch checkpoint instead?
ryan: tokenizer diff snippet: ```diff
- "eos_id": 1,
+ "eos_id": 2,
  "normalize_unicode": false -> true
```
sophia: that + normalize toggle explains slight tokenization skew. would prefer model-onboard adjust checkpoint if possible; but runtime guard is safer short-term.
marta: marking this a rollout-blocker until either kernel selector fix or checkpoint revert lands. prioritizing oncall for hotfix.
kevin: assigning self. ETA for PR: ~3h. will run A/B with shadow traffic once ready.
sophia: thanks everyone. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
